pro_show-215.html.html:
This machine is a complete multi-strand twisting unit specially designed for manufacturing high-quality control cables and fiber optic cables. Redesigned with reference to advanced cabling equipment at home and abroad and combined with the actual requirements of wire and cable production, the machine consists of a pay-off stand, wire guide die holder, central wrapping unit, serving unit, rotating length counter, cantilever-arm tub twister and safety guards.

The machine is controlled by a PLC program. Frequency-converter motor controllers keep the output shaft speed essentially constant, with stepless adjustment via the computer. All parameters can be set freely from the operator panel, and the operating interface does not interfere with the main machine. Acceleration and deceleration are highly linear, with a lay error within 2%. Automatic meter counting is provided; when the preset length is reached, the main machine and the wrapping unit automatically decelerate smoothly to a stop.

China's Optical and Electrical Cable Industry Will Still Maintain 20% Rapid Growth During the 13th Five-Year Plan Period

On May 29, the “Outline of the 13th Five-Year Development Plan for China's Optical and Electrical Cable and Optical Device Industry” was released. The Outline proposes that by the end of the 13th Five-Year Plan period, China's optical and electrical cable industry will complete an industrial output value of RMB 640.758 billion, a year-on-year increase of 20%, with recommended R&D expenditure equal to 5% of that year's gross industrial output value, reaching RMB 32.037 billion by the end of the period.

According to the introduction, the Outline is structured on a 1+16 principle: one master plan plus 16 major categories of specialized products. The 300,000-word planning report presents detailed data across all categories in a clear and well-organized manner.

Over the past five years, Chinese optical and electrical cable and optical device enterprises have closely followed the national development strategy and made strenuous efforts centered on innovation-driven growth and transformation, achieving encouraging results. Relevant data show that by the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, the industry's industrial output value had increased by 26% year on year, and its tax contribution to the state reached RMB 90.007 billion. The 31 listed companies in the industry posted total sales of RMB 220.578 billion, accounting for 41.3% of the entire sector. The boundaries of industrial capital are clearly defined, and a structure dominated by private enterprises plus listed companies has basically taken shape. As the industrial structure continues to improve, the market competitiveness of the five major segments — optical fiber preforms, optical fiber and cable, optical devices, strategic emerging industries, and traditional coaxial cables, data cables, railway signal cables and high-frequency electronic cable assemblies — continues to strengthen.

In optical fiber preforms, optical fiber and optical cable, China broke the foreign monopoly on optical fiber preforms by the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, raising the domestic production rate from less than 30% to about 80%. Preform technology achieved breakthroughs across the board, and total domestic preform capacity now exceeds 5,000 tons. Manufacturing equipment for optical fiber preforms based on independent intellectual property has been successfully developed, and the total scale has reached RMB 93.5 billion. Optical fiber and cable production capacity is ample, supplying more than half of the global market. Annual capacities for optical fiber and optical cable stand at 240 million km and 280 million fiber-km respectively. There are more than 150 enterprises in total, including about 40 larger optical cable companies, about 20 companies capable of producing both optical fiber and cable, and about 10 companies integrated across optical fiber preform, fiber and cable. China has become the world's largest producer of optical fiber and cable by capacity, and a number of leading enterprises have joined the ranks of international leaders. Complete sets of optical fiber drawing equipment have been localized, and some of this equipment is now being sold overseas. Welded pipe production lines for optical units such as OPGW, OPPC and submarine optical cable have basically achieved domestic production. By the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, this industry cluster had completed sales revenue of RMB 133.063 billion, accounting for 24.9% of the entire sector.

China's optical device industry has also entered a new round of growth. During the 12th Five-Year Plan period, there were more than 300 optical device manufacturers in China, including about 90 makers of active optical devices, more than 180 of passive optical devices, and about 30 of modules and subsystems as well as wafers and chips. The industry employed 65,000 people. Optical device sales reached 11.3 billion units, with an output value of RMB 52.4 billion. By the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, this industry cluster's total sales revenue had reached RMB 12.1 billion, accounting for 2% of the entire sector.

Optical and electrical cables for strategic emerging industry equipment have emerged as a new force. This segment, together with optical devices, is a major supplier and support provider for emerging industries such as energy and information interconnection networks, and is expected to become an important lever for innovation-driven growth and economic transformation as well as a new engine for “stabilizing growth.” The plan subdivides this emerging industry into nine major product clusters — rail transit vehicles, electric vehicles, marine engineering equipment, industrial robots, photovoltaics, wind turbines, nuclear power, military applications and data. By the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, these clusters had completed a total output value of RMB 10 billion, accounting for 1.8% of the entire sector. Products also include coaxial cables, data cables, railway signal cables and installation wires. By the end of the 12th Five-Year Plan period, annual sales revenue of coaxial cables reached RMB 23.902 billion, and that of railway signal cables reached RMB 2.6 billion. Domestic production bases for high-frequency electronic cable assemblies are mainly concentrated in the Pearl River Delta, Yangtze River Delta and Bohai Rim regions; this cluster has a total scale of RMB 329.5 billion, accounting for 61% of the entire sector.

The Outline notes that entering the 13th Five-Year Plan period, the optical and electrical cable and electronic components industry must, through supply-side reform, elevate its development horizon from the domestic market to a global market position, and grasp industry trends from the perspective of the global manufacturing value chain. The guiding philosophy for the industry's 13th Five-Year development must center on seeking progress while maintaining stability and on balanced development, enhancing independent innovation capability through introduction, digestion, absorption and re-innovation, with emphasis on cutting overcapacity, adjusting structure, shoring up weaknesses and raising efficiency. The industry should embrace “Internet Plus” and new smart manufacturing technologies to further strengthen its overall capability across the complete industrial chain from R&D and manufacturing to marketing and operational services.

The Outline also proposes that the whole industry work hard to cut overcapacity and shore up weaknesses while optimizing the industrial structure. During the 13th Five-Year Plan period, qualified enterprises are encouraged to relocate excess capacity overseas, while special attention must be paid to addressing the weak links in the industrial sector. A “quality revolution” is the inevitable path for “Made in China.” In the industry development plan, we have already laid out key priorities in areas such as standards capability, certification body development, brand building, and the creation of intellectual property for well-known trademarks.

The Outline further calls for concentrating superior resources on shoring up weaknesses in raw and auxiliary materials, equipment and high-end manufacturing. The planning report notes the weak link that the development of industry talent resources is not commensurate with industry growth and cannot meet the needs of specialized development. The industry should embrace the Internet and achieve new breakthroughs in smart manufacturing. By the end of the 13th Five-Year Plan period, the rise of smart manufacturing will become the new engine of the next revolution in the optical and electrical cable industry. (Source: People's Daily Online)

As electric vehicles gain in popularity, the EV charging pile industry is also booming, and charging performance has become a matter of widespread concern. Fast charging demands high power and high current, yet a cable that carries current for long periods tends to heat up. The quality of charging pile cables is therefore critical, because it is directly related to charging safety.

The voltage rating for high-voltage cables was originally 60 V. In response to market changes and demand, this has now risen to as high as 1,500 V, and the increase from 60 V to 1,500 V places far higher demands on cables. Likewise, automotive conductors have grown from 25 mm² to high-voltage cables of 50 mm², 75 mm², 95 mm² and 120 mm². As cable cross-sections have increased, the required voltage withstand ratings have risen accordingly.

Traditional wire and cable machinery manufacturers have never produced conductors of such large cross-sections and cannot achieve the corresponding voltage withstand ratings. Conversely, the companies capable of manufacturing large-cross-section conductors are not part of the automotive supply chain and know little about the product requirements and delivery standards of the automotive industry. Both the companies within the automotive supply chain and the cable manufacturers outside it are searching for ways to break through.

Manufacturing large-cross-section high-voltage cables to such demanding standards requires advanced equipment. With more than 22 years of experience in the production of wire and cable machinery and over 60 national invention and utility-model patents, Qingfeng is one of the leading domestic manufacturers of professional high-end cable equipment. We can custom-build complete extrusion lines to customer requirements, suitable for new-energy charging pile cables, new-energy special cables and related applications.

As new energy vehicles become widespread, the supply gap in high-voltage cables will draw many conventional cable producers into the automotive supply chain, while the demands on companies already in that supply chain will keep growing. With strong national emphasis on the new energy vehicle market, the share of new-energy high-voltage cables in China's cable market is expected to rise. At the same time, the automotive high-voltage cable market will go through a phase of survival of the fittest and accelerated consolidation of resources.

High-Temperature Resistance

Under high-temperature conditions, the deformation and ageing of the wire or cable is slowed. Conventional wires and cables are rated for continuous working temperatures of around 70-90 °C. The newer 105 °C and 125 °C wire products made from upgraded materials can easily cope with heavy household loads or conditions such as temporary short circuits.

Ageing Resistance

Under mechanical, electrical and thermal stresses and various other external factors, wires and cables must retain their original performance, resisting ageing so as to prolong service life. All wires and cables offer some ageing resistance, but the better the quality, the slower the ageing and the longer the service life.

Corrosion Resistance

Cables must resist electrochemical corrosion, biological attack, chemical agents (oils, acids, alkalis, chemical solvents, etc.), salt spray, sunlight and low temperatures, and must also offer anti-fungal and moisture-proof properties. In service, wires and cables inevitably come into contact with air, water, acidic substances and the like. Corrosion resistance limits the rate and extent of the corrosion and weathering caused by such exposure, while also slowing ageing and extending service life.

Flame Retardance

This property means that, in the event of an electrical fire, the wire or cable does not readily ignite; and if it does continue to burn, the spread of flame along the cable is greatly reduced. Once removed from the source of the fire, it extinguishes on its own.

Some electrical fires in China start when a short circuit ignites a section of wire or cable, after which the fire travels continuously along the cable run and develops into a major blaze. Flame-retardant wires and cables minimise this risk by preventing the spread of flame.

Fire Resistance

The difference between fire-resistant and flame-retardant wires and cables is that a fire-resistant cable continues to operate safely for a specified period when exposed to flame, maintaining the integrity of the circuit. Such cables are mainly used in high-rise buildings, underground railways, underground shopping streets, large power stations and important industrial and mining enterprises — wherever fire safety and fire-fighting and evacuation functions are essential.

In 2020, China produced 25.225 million vehicles. At an estimated wiring harness value of RMB 2,000 per vehicle, the annual output value of China's automotive electronic wiring harness products exceeds RMB 50 billion. The automotive wiring harness industry is highly dependent on the automotive sector. Most brand-name automakers have established mature and stable component supply systems; international automakers — particularly the German, American and Japanese manufacturers — subject their component suppliers to strict assessment and evaluation. Their long-standing high standards for components have kept the relationship between wiring harness suppliers and automakers relatively stable.

In recent years, as international automakers pay increasing attention to cost control, localised sourcing of automotive components has steadily strengthened, and a number of excellent domestic wiring harness manufacturers have emerged. Through many years of accumulated product technology and synchronous-development experience, these quality local companies have significantly strengthened their overall capabilities and, backed by timely and effective service and reliable product quality, have gradually entered the supplier systems of international automakers.

In the fast-growing new energy vehicle sector, the wiring harness is one of the most important components, mainly comprising body harnesses, BMS (Battery Management System) harnesses and energy storage harnesses. Because the lithium batteries used in new energy vehicles are rather unstable, the battery management system, as the core technology, plays a decisive role. Of all these harnesses, the BMS harness is the most critical one, functioning as the nerve centre of the vehicle.

BMS harnesses are subject to demanding requirements: they must be short, compact, light, thin and flexible, while also carrying high currents and providing dust-proof, water-proof and interference-resistant performance.

In electric vehicles, the connectors and cables of the high-voltage harness are critical interconnection components during vehicle operation. The main hazards affecting high-voltage harnesses are overheating or burning, in addition to harsh environmental exposure, shielding performance, and the risk of water or dust ingress.

China's new energy vehicle industry has made remarkable progress, and new energy vehicles of every kind have gradually entered our daily lives. These include battery electric vehicles, extended-range electric vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles, fuel-cell electric vehicles, hydrogen-engine vehicles and other new energy vehicle types. In any new energy vehicle, whether a hybrid or a fully electric model, the high-voltage system is one of the core parts, and its importance is self-evident. As the medium that interconnects the components of the high-voltage system, the high-voltage wiring harness likewise plays an indispensable role.

■Conductor Structure Design (Very Important)

Conductors are normally built from a single strand or multiple strands, and are classified by material as bare copper, tinned copper, silver-plated copper, copper foil yarn, copper-clad steel and the like. The finer and softer the conductor, the better its flexing performance.

To improve flex life, conductors are usually built up from multiple strands, with fillers such as nylon yarn or Kevlar (ballistic yarn) added where necessary. For stranded conductors, the shorter the lay length, the better the flexing performance.

■Insulation Structure Design (Important)

Insulation protects and insulates the conductor. Insulation materials include FEP, PTFE, nylon, shrink-resistant PP, the PE family (low-density LDPE, medium-density MDPE and high-density HDPE), semi-rigid SR-PVC, PVC, Foam PE (not recommended for cables to be subjected to flexing tests) and Foam PE + skin (also not recommended for flexing-test cables), among others.

In terms of insulation materials, and with all other conditions being equal, the more cost-effective choices are FEP or PTFE insulation, followed by Hytrel, then nylon, then shrink-resistant PP (not ordinary PP), and then the PE family. Where keeping costs to a minimum is the deciding factor, the PVC series is the choice.

If the insulation wall is too thin, the conductor is not adequately protected; if it is too thick, the cable becomes too stiff. For video-signal cables such as DP (DisplayPort) and HDMI, the internal foamed signal conductors tend to break during flexing because foamed materials have poor flex resistance. For such cables, flexing performance is mainly improved through the conductor lay length, the construction and the filling of the stranded bundle.

■Filling/Spacing Structure Design (General)

Filling serves two purposes: it maintains the roundness of the cable, and it protects the cable from damage during bending, thereby contributing to flex resistance. Common fillers include nylon yarn (ballistic yarn), Kevlar, cotton yarn, PP jute-fibre filler, hemp rope, PVC filler rods and the like.

In order of flex resistance, Kevlar out-performs nylon yarn (ballistic yarn), nylon yarn out-performs cotton yarn, cotton yarn out-performs PP jute-fibre filler and hemp rope, and PP jute-fibre filler and hemp rope out-perform PVC filler rods.

When filling, nylon yarn (ballistic yarn) and Kevlar are usually used inside the conductor or during stranding; cotton yarn, PP jute-fibre filler, hemp rope and PVC filler rods are usually used as filling material during stranding.

■Separation/Bedding Layer (General)

A. Separation materials commonly include aluminium foil, PET tape, foamed PP tape, non-woven fabric and the like, used mainly in the bundling/cabling stage.

B. Because foamed PP tape and non-woven fabric are thicker and softer, they provide better flex resistance than other separation materials. However, being thicker and more costly, they are generally used in cables with electrical performance requirements or where the overall OD can accommodate them.

C. Isolation tapes are generally applied either longitudinally or helically, among which helical taping offers better flex resistance than longitudinal taping. The final choice, however, depends on the cable construction.

■Jacket (Primary)

The jacket directly protects the entire inner structure of the cable. As a general rule, a thicker jacket is better than a thinner one, a softer material better than a harder one, and a loose (tube-type) extrusion better than a tight (pressure-type) extrusion.

Jackets are mostly PVC, although TPU, TPE and other materials are also used. Since TPE and TPU offer better elongation and elasticity than PVC, they also provide better flexing performance.

High-frequency data cables are mainly used to transmit data signals. Diffraction, obstruction and atmospheric absorption, however, are all frequency-dependent: the higher the frequency, the more readily the signal is blocked and absorbed. High-frequency signals therefore tend to suffer a drop in signal strength (voltage) caused by the resistance of the base material, while the aluminium foil layer protects and shields the information being transmitted, reducing interference from extraneous external signals on the transmission.

The main wrapping material, aluminium-foil Mylar, is a laminated aluminium-plastic composite foil that exploits the airtightness and shielding properties of aluminium foil and serves as the cable shield. The taping machine assembles the two insulated cores and the drain wire, then wraps the bundle with a layer of aluminium-foil Mylar and a layer of self-adhesive polyester tape, providing shielding for the pair and stabilising the wrapped core structure.

When analysing transmission line losses, attention should also be paid to the skin effect, the proximity effect, surface roughness, the complex permittivity of the dielectric, dielectric loss, and the frequency-dependent characteristics of impedance and time delay. The conductor's own losses are the principal component of high-frequency attenuation: they arise mainly from the resistance of the conductor itself, and under an AC signal the impedance of the conductor varies with frequency. The surface of the trace always has a certain degree of roughness, and when the wavelength of the signal approaches the scale of this roughness, resistive losses are aggravated. Moreover, because of the skin effect, high-frequency current concentrates on the surface of the conductor, further increasing the impedance losses of the conductor. Below we analyse how these losses manifest themselves on the transmission line.

Low cable attenuation can be attributed to the following factors:

a. A large centre conductor diameter (d), or a large diameter of the dielectric insulating material.
The dielectric material must be able to retain the high-frequency energy and prevent it from dissipating through the resistive components.
The lower the dissipation factor of the dielectric material, the higher its ability to transmit high-frequency energy.

b. Low resistance of the centre conductor or its coating.

c. A low dielectric constant.

d. A low skin-effect depth.

An extruder production line operator is the person primarily responsible for maintaining the equipment and prolonging the service life of the extruder. Every operator should understand that reducing the frequency of repairs and parts replacement and extending the working life of the extruder is an important technical measure for lowering the production management costs of plastic products and improving overall economic efficiency. Keeping the equipment operating at its best over the long term, with stable plastic quality and output, is the basic condition that ensures safe production and sound profitability.

When operators follow the operating procedures conscientiously and take full responsibility for their work, that in itself is the best maintenance and care the equipment can receive. New workers must therefore learn and memorise the extruder operating procedures before going on duty, and may operate the equipment independently only after passing an actual hands-on operating examination.

To work on your own and become a qualified extruder operator, you should pay attention to the following items.

(1) Shift handover
Any problems encountered with the equipment during the shift must be clearly communicated to the next shift. Record the production output, product quality and equipment status in the shift handover log.

(2) At the start of the shift
After completing the handover procedures, first check the production quality of the products, verify the quality of the raw materials, and check the amount of material in the extruder hopper. Report any problems to the supervisor without delay.

(3) Check whether the barrel and the process control temperatures of the extruder are within the process temperature ranges required for production. Depending on the product quality, appropriate adjustments may be made based on your own operating experience.

(4) Routine inspection
Walk a full circuit around the equipment and check the condition of the drive components while it is running: observe whether the rotation is smooth and normal, listen for any abnormal operating sounds, and check whether the temperatures of the heated zones are normal.

(5) Check the gauges: on the operating control box, read the main motor voltage and current. The ammeter pointer should be within the normal rated current range.

(6) When production is running normally, the extruder screw rotates steadily and the plastic product is extruded smoothly and uniformly from the die head. At intervals, inspect the appearance of the product, or take samples and test whether all its parameters meet the requirements.

(7) In the event of a sudden power failure during operation, immediately switch off the main motor, the heating and the material feed system, and return all speed-adjustment controls to zero. When power is restored, first reheat the barrel to the required process temperature and hold it there for a period of time. Turn the screw by hand through the motor and belt connection to gauge the resistance. If it turns relatively easily, start the motor at low speed and resume work. If the ammeter pointer exceeds the rated current, or the screw speed is not steady on starting, stop the line promptly, investigate the cause (the material in the barrel may not have reached temperature), identify and rectify the fault, and only then restart the machine.

(8) If the machine is to be shut down for a long period, no cleaning is needed if the material remaining in the barrel is a polyolefin type. However, if the barrel contains nylon/polyamide or similar materials, the barrel must be cleared of the remaining material. The screw should then be removed and cleaned, together with the barrel, removing all residue from the screw and the barrel. After cleaning, coat the screw with a layer of anti-rust oil, wrap it well and hang it vertically in a dry, well-ventilated place.

news_show-22.html.html:
Stranding machines have a very wide range of applications. Apart from the standard stranding machine, automatic and fully automatic stranding machines can all wind coils of different sizes, such as toroidal (ring) coils and square coils — the two most common types. These types differ mainly in their winding settings: every type of coil must be set with the appropriate basic parameters, and the tension, wire-guiding and other techniques must also be adjusted in good time, so that the wound coils meet the process requirements and achieve the distinctive appearance required.

When winding fine coils, a stranding machine generally uses one of two traverse methods: free (random) layering and forced (positive) layering. Each method has its own advantages. Free layering relies on the surface tension of the wire and the oscillation of the guide wheel or pendulum to lay the wire. Since the guide rollers are set some distance away from the coil structure, with the right adjustment every turn can be laid tightly against the previous one, so that the finished coil can achieve the desired mirror-glass effect. However, adjustment is very difficult, mainly because of the large number of control variables on the machine. Forced layering uses the coordinated motion of the machine spindle and the traverse mechanism, so that for each revolution of the coil the traverse moves forward by a fixed distance, usually one wire diameter per turn. With today's CNC technology this is not hard to implement: once the winding parameters have been set in advance, winding can be carried out without much adjustment. However, sustained testing has shown that the forced layering method is very difficult to use when rapidly winding coils with wire of less than 0.1 mm, and scrambled winding frequently occurs.

A Dongguan stranding machine manufacturer must first analyse the situation and determine which category a problem belongs to. Taking a traverse-type stranding machine as an example, several common problems are described below.

1. Untidy wire layering. Analyse the specific situation to determine whether the problem occurs during normal production or after a product change and the subsequent adjustment. The former is generally a system configuration problem, while the latter is usually a settings problem. Configuration problems are typically caused by loose clamping fixtures, loose fixing screws on the traverse mechanism, or poor lubrication of the traverse mechanism, which overloads the AC servomotor and causes it to lose steps, resulting in untidy layering.

2. Inaccurate stopping position of the machine spindle. This is usually caused by a fault in the brake. For example, the brake pads may be loose or worn out. It is also related to the brake time setting: if the brake time is too short, the spindle will not stop at the required position. The brake pads must be replaced, or the brake timing adjusted.

3. Inaccurate coil-turn counting. If an inaccurate count occurs in a traverse-type stranding machine, it is generally caused by a configuration problem with the sensor or the controller. When this happens, the stranding machine cannot operate, and the Dongguan stranding machine manufacturer should generally be called in to repair it.

news_show-23.html.html:
Cage-type and frame-type stranding machines are constantly compared with each other. Today, let's take a look at the differences between the two.

I. Production speed
Frame-type strander: because it adopts a frame structure, the central shaft is not loaded by the weight of the reels, so the machine has high rigidity. It offers good overall performance, a small turning radius and a high production speed.
Cage-type strander: its small turning radius and the complex structure of its de-twisting device limit the production speed of the cage-type strander.

II. De-twisting capability
Frame-type strander: the frame-type strander cannot de-twist. During stranding, the individual wires acquire torsional stress, so that high-toughness hard-drawn round conductors are not laid tightly and easily spread apart. For this reason, some frame-type stranders are fitted with a pre-forming device ahead of the stranding cage to eliminate the torsional stress in the individual wires.
Cage-type strander: it carries out de-twisting stranding by means of a de-twisting ring, chain or sprocket arrangements and planetary gear de-twisting mechanisms, making it suitable for individual elements that cannot withstand torque, such as optical fibres. Cage-type stranders must be used for high-toughness round wires (such as aluminium-clad steel wires) and for rope-lay stranded cores.

III. Stranding of insulated cable cores
Frame-type strander: because it cannot perform de-twisting stranding, it can only be used for stranding solid-conductor insulated cores of small sizes.
Cage-type strander: it can perform stranding with or without de-twisting and is suitable for all kinds of insulated cable cores.

IV. Tension control
Frame-type strander: tension control is achieved by mechanical friction or pneumatic methods.

However, the strap length must then be re-adjusted to ensure that the next wrapping proceeds normally. The installation, adjustment and test running of the machine are generally specified in the instruction manual of the extruder. The operating method, maintenance and care of the extruder are briefly described below.

I. Operating Method of the Extruder

Operators must be thoroughly familiar with the structural characteristics of the extruder they operate, especially the structural characteristics of the screw, the characteristics of the heating and cooling control instruments, and the characteristics and assembly of the die head, so that they can correctly establish the extrusion process conditions and operate the machine properly.

The operating methods for extruding different plastic products differ, but there are also points in common. The steps common to the extrusion of all kinds of products and the precautions to be observed during operation are briefly introduced below.

1. Preparations before starting

(1) Plastics used for extrusion should meet the required drying requirements, and further drying should be carried out where necessary. Screen the raw material to remove lumps, agglomerates and mechanical impurities.

(2) Check that the water, power and air systems of the equipment are normal, and ensure that the water and air lines are unobstructed and leak-free, the electrical system is normal, and the heating system, temperature controls and all instruments operate reliably. Run the auxiliary machines at low speed with no load to observe whether the equipment operates normally. Start the vacuum pump of the sizing table and check that it operates normally. Add lubricant to all lubrication points of the equipment. Rectify any fault as soon as it is found.

(3) Mount the die head and sizing sleeve. Select the appropriate die head specification according to the type and size of the product. Assemble the die head in the following order.

1. The die head should be assembled as a whole unit and mounted on the extruder.
2. Before assembling the die head, wipe off the grease applied for storage, carefully check whether the surfaces of the mould cavity are dented, scratched or rusted, polish them where necessary, and then apply a layer of silicone oil on the flow channel surfaces.
3. Assemble the plates of the die head in order, apply high-temperature grease to the threads of the bolts, and then tighten the bolts and flanges.
4. Place the breaker plate between the die-head flanges so that it is securely held and no material leaks.
5. Before tightening the fastening bolts of the die head and the extruder connecting flange, level the die. A level can be used to level a square die head, while a round die head should be levelled against the rubber base of the sizing tool using the base of the die opening.
6. Tighten the connecting flange bolts and the die-head fastening bolts, and install the heating bands and thermocouples. Make sure the heating bands fit tightly against the outer surface of the die head.
7. Install and position the sizing sleeve, and check that the centre lines of the main machine, the sizing sleeve and the haul-off machine are aligned. After adjustment, tighten the fixing bolts. Connect the water pipes and vacuum tubes of the sizing sleeve.
8. Switch on the heating power and heat the die head and barrel evenly. At the same time, open the cooling water at the bottom of the hopper and at the gearbox, and the water inlet valve of the exhausting vacuum pump. During heating, set the temperature of each zone to 140 °C first. When the temperature reaches 140 °C, hold it for 30-40 minutes, and then raise the temperature to that of normal production. After the temperature reaches the normal production temperature, hold it for about 10 minutes so that the temperatures of all parts of the machine become stable before starting production. The holding time varies with the model of the extruder and the type of plastic material. The material should be soaked (held at temperature) for a period so that the inside and outside temperatures of the machine are consistent; otherwise, when the indicating instrument has reached the required temperature but the actual temperature is still on the low side, charging material into the extruder at the too-low actual temperature will make the melt viscosity too high, causing overload of the axial force and damage to the machine.
9. Feed the raw material for starting into the hopper, ready for use.

2. Starting

(1) The machine can be started after the temperature has been kept constant. Before starting, retighten the flange bolts of the die head and the extruder to eliminate the difference between the thermal expansion of the bolts and the die head. Tighten the die-head bolts diagonally, exerting even force. When tightening the flange nuts of the die head, the tightness around the whole circumference must be even; otherwise material will leak.

(2) To start the machine, first press the Ready for Start button, then the Start button. Then slowly rotate the screw speed adjustment knob to start the screw at low speed, and gradually increase the speed while adding material a little at a time. While feeding material, pay close attention to the main motor ammeter and the indications of the various indicating gauges. The screw torque must not exceed the red mark (generally 65%-75% of the torque gauge). Before the plastic profile is extruded, no one may stand directly in front of the die opening, to prevent injury accidents caused by bolt breakage or by the material bubbling owing to dampness. Once the plastic is extruded from the die opening, the extrudate should be cooled slowly and threaded onto the haul-off device and into the sizing die, and these devices started. Then, according to the readings of the control instruments and the requirements for the extruded product, adjust the various parts accordingly so that the whole extrusion operation reaches a normal state. Add sufficient material as required. For twin-screw extruders, use a metering feeder to feed material uniformly and at a constant rate.

(3) When the material is issuing evenly from the die and is well plastified, the extrudate can be drawn into the sizing sleeve. The degree of plastification is judged by experience, generally from the appearance of the extrudate: the surface should be glossy, free of impurities, without foaming, scorched material or discolouration; when the extrudate is squeezed thin by hand it should show no burrs or cracks and should have a certain elasticity — this indicates good plastification. If plastification is poor, the screw speed and the barrel and die-head temperatures may be adjusted as required until the requirement is met.

(4) During the extrusion process, the various process parameters should be checked regularly according to the process requirements to confirm that they are normal, and the process record sheet should be completed. Inspect the quality of the profile products against the quality inspection standard, and take corrective measures as soon as any problem is found.

3. Stopping

(1) Stop feeding, extrude all the plastic remaining in the extruder until the screw is exposed, and then switch off the power to the barrel and die head to stop heating.

(2) Switch off the power to the extruder and the auxiliary machines so that the screw and the auxiliaries stop running.

(3) Open the connecting flange of the die head and remove the die head. Clean the breaker plate and the various parts of the die head. To prevent damage to the inner surfaces of the die head during cleaning, the residual material in the die head should be removed with steel strips and blades, and the plastic adhering inside the die head should then be ground off with sandpaper, polished, and coated with machine oil or silicone oil to prevent rust.

(4) Cleaning of the screw and barrel: after removing the die head, restart the main machine and feed stopping material (or regrind) to clean the screw and barrel, running the screw at low speed (around a few tens of r/min) to reduce wear. After the stopping material is fully extruded and reduced to powder, use compressed air to blow the residual pellets and powder out through the feed opening and the vent opening repeatedly, until it is confirmed that no residue remains in the barrel. Then reduce the screw speed to zero, stop the extruder, and switch off the main power and the main cooling water valve.

(5) The safety items to be noted during extrusion include electricity, heat, rotating mechanical parts and the handling of heavy parts. The extrusion workshop must be equipped with lifting equipment for the assembly and disassembly of the die head, screw and other heavy parts, to ensure safe production.

II. Maintenance and Care of the Extruder

The screw extrusion system is maintained and serviced in two ways: routine maintenance and periodic maintenance.

(1) Routine maintenance is an ongoing routine task that does not occupy equipment operating hours and is normally completed during running. The focus is on cleaning the machine, lubricating the moving parts, tightening threaded parts that tend to work loose, and promptly checking and adjusting the motors, control instruments, working parts and pipes.

(2) Periodic maintenance is generally carried out after the extruder has run continuously for 2,500-5,000 hours, when the machine is stopped and dismantled for inspection, measurement and assessment of the wear of the main parts; parts that have worn to the specified limit should be replaced, and damaged parts repaired.

(3) Do not run the machine idle, to avoid scoring of the screw and barrel.

(4) If any abnormal sound occurs while the extruder is running, stop immediately for inspection or repair.

(5) Strictly prevent metal or other foreign matter from falling into the hopper, to avoid damaging the screw and barrel. To prevent ferrous foreign matter from entering the barrel, a magnetic catcher or magnetic frame may be installed at the feed opening where the material enters the barrel; to prevent foreign matter from falling in, the material must be screened beforehand.

(6) Keep the production environment clean; do not let rubbish or impurities mix into the material and block the filter/breaker plate, which would affect the output and quality of the product and increase the resistance of the die head.

(7) When the extruder is to be out of service for a long period, apply anti-rust grease to the working surfaces of the screw, barrel, die head and other parts. Small screws should be suspended in the air or placed in a dedicated wooden case, padded level with wooden blocks, to avoid deformation or damage.

(8) Calibrate the temperature control instruments regularly and check the correctness of their adjustment and the sensitivity of their control.

(9) The gearbox of the extruder is maintained in the same way as a standard reduction gearbox, mainly by checking the gears, bearings and other parts for wear and failure. The gearbox should use the lubricating oil specified in the machine manual, filled to the specified oil level. Too little oil results in insufficient lubrication and shortens the service life of the parts; too much oil generates excessive heat, consumes more energy and makes the oil deteriorate easily, likewise causing lubrication failure and damage to the parts. Seals (gaskets or rings) at any leaking points of the gearbox should be replaced promptly to ensure the correct lubricating oil quantity.

(10) The inner walls of the cooling water pipes attached to the extruder tend to scale, and the outer surfaces tend to corrode and rust. Careful inspection should be carried out during maintenance: excessive scale blocks the pipes and prevents effective cooling, while severe corrosion causes water leakage. Descaling and anti-corrosion measures must therefore be taken during maintenance.

(11) For the DC motor that drives the screw, pay special attention to the wear and contact condition of the brushes. The insulation resistance of the motor should also be measured regularly to confirm that it is above the specified value. In addition, check whether the connecting wires and other parts are rusted, and take protective measures.

(12) Assign a specific person to be responsible for equipment maintenance and care, and record every maintenance and repair in detail in the factory equipment management file.

High-speed stranding machines have evolved from hand-cranked, to automatic, to fully automatic operation over the past half century. A fully automatic high-speed stranding machine must necessarily incorporate a wide range of automation technologies, mainly including control systems, transmission control, motion control, industrial touch screens and sensors. Driven by market demand, fully automatic high-speed stranding machines are now the most widely used type, although the market has long since taken on a flourishing and highly diversified landscape. So what are the adjustment methods for the spindle of a fully automatic high-speed stranding machine? Our stranding machine manufacturer will introduce them below.

The stranding machine manufacturer

Many purchasers of fully automatic high-speed stranding machines simply use the equipment according to the layout and configuration set at delivery, just as they would follow a car dealership's arrangement. Some customers, however, need to change the position or function of certain components to suit their own production process. When a fully automatic high-speed stranding machine is designed and manufactured, a certain amount of space is generally reserved to facilitate convenient maintenance and the dismantling of components. Customers can use this space to make certain improvements, but every improvement must stay within the maximum limits permitted by the equipment. Making blind, arbitrary modifications to the equipment can damage it.

The spindle of a fully automatic high-speed stranding machine is the drive shaft that applies rotational force to turn the wire being stranded. Machines of different sizes have different spindle configurations. Spindle adjustment generally covers the following aspects: the shaft outlet position, coaxiality adjustment, and supplementary winding process settings. The shaft outlet position usually needs adjustment when, during the winding stage, the clearance between the spindle and the machine table does not meet the production process requirements, since every production stage requires a certain working space. When adjusting the shaft outlet position, pay attention to the size of the opening on the main frame and whether the adjustment will affect the normal operation of other components. Coaxiality adjustment is common: after a period of operation, the coaxiality between the winding reel and the mold pin on a fully automatic high-speed stranding machine may deviate, and it must be inspected and adjusted as soon as possible.

Adjustment of the wire traversing device mainly covers the traverse interval and the rotation diameter. The traverse interval is adjusted when the starting winding point does not match the winding process. The usual method is to move the machine's homing sensor, but bear in mind that the movement must not exceed the machine's mechanical starting point; leave as much clearance as possible so that the equipment cannot cause a mechanical collision when returning to its home position. Since adjustment methods differ from one stranding machine manufacturer to another, customers should contact their supplier in good time before making adjustments and master the key adjustment steps.

There are many kinds of magnet wire coils, using a wide variety of winding wires and with diverse requirements. For some magnet coil products with special requirements, domestic manufacturers were once forced to give up one after another. After years of absorbing and digesting the technology, the process capability of fully automatic high-speed stranding machines has been steadily improving, and even models with special requirements can now be handled much more easily. As stranding machine manufacturers' production capacity grows, customization lead times are also getting shorter.

The above is what the stranding machine manufacturer has explained about spindle adjustment methods for fully automatic high-speed stranding machines. We believe that through today's content you now understand these adjustment methods, and we hope it is useful to you.

Since no stranding is required, the process by which transmission line pairs are formed into cables is in fact completed on the wrapping machine. The tension control of every part of the wrapping machine is the key factor that determines its quality. For SFP high-speed transmission lines, the wrapping machine should have at least the following components: an active pay-off unit with stable tension, a concentric double-layer winding unit, a hot-melt unit, and a take-up unit with stable tension. The technical control points of each functional unit are analyzed below.

The strap length is adjusted by the strap length adjuster on the front plate. If the strap is too short, it is easy to wind up around the operator's hands. In this case, firmly grasp the strap end and pull the strap out along its direction on the wrapping machine; however, the strap length must be re-adjusted to ensure the next tying operation proceeds normally. If the strap is too long, it is hard to position, and the loose strap is easily tangled, resulting in inaccurate tying or strap breakage. Maintenance:

1. Keep the inside of the machine clean and dry at all times.

2. Prevent moisture or dirt from accumulating on the machine tabletop.

3. The power cord should be kept clear of moving parts and should be coiled up when not in use.

4. Keep the machine running normally and select quality raw material strapping straps.

Main features of the wrapping machine equipment.

1. The wrapping machine adopts separate motor control, achieving high speed, low noise and no oil leakage, which also keeps the workshop environment clean. Alternatively, it can use ground-shaft drive (the gearbox is a high-speed six-speed gearbox offering forward, reverse and neutral gears, linked to the ground shaft of the main drive, providing high speed, low noise and high production capacity).

2. The wrapping device has a flat structure. The strap payout angle is adjusted by guide rollers, each reel can be adjusted independently, and the strap tension is controlled by mechanical friction with automatic adjustment.

3. Braking is by pneumatic disc brake, giving a good and smooth braking effect.

4. The caterpillar-type haul-off unit has a built-in 4-speed gearbox and is linked to the winding machine through encoder signals, ensuring a stable and reliable winding pitch.

5. The wrapping head is fitted with a high-strength integral base plate, making installation and adjustment easy and operation reliable. It eliminates the defect of foundation settlement and ensures the machine's accuracy during transport.

6. The wrapping machine has a scientific and rational structural design, well-selected materials and fine workmanship, with a low failure rate, and it can meet the requirements of long-term, high-intensity continuous production.

The wrapping machine equipment is mainly used for the non-metallic wrapping of various cables. After parts adjustment, it can also be used to produce copper tape shielding, thin copper tape and steel tape armoring.

news_show-28.html.html:
1. Problems encountered by the extrusion machine during production:

Plastic scorching. Plastic scorching is a common quality defect in the plastic extrusion process. Its main symptoms are: an excessively high temperature reading; heavy smoke and a strong, pungent odor at the die, with crackling or popping in serious cases; scorched particles in the extruded plastic layer; and continuous bubbles at the weld seam. The main causes are:

- The temperature control is set too high, reaching the thermal degradation temperature of the plastic.
- The screw has not been cleaned for a long time, so the scorched material that has built up is forced out together with the molten plastic.
- The heating or stopping time is too long, so the plastic remains in the barrel for too long and degrades from the heat.
- The temperature control instrument fails or is inaccurate, causing high-temperature degradation.

The cooling system of the extrusion machine is not switched on, causing the material to overheat from shear friction. During extrusion, therefore, you should step up checks to confirm that the heating and cooling systems are operating properly; allow the extrusion temperatures to be set according to the process requirements and the screw speed; reasonably control the heating time; and clean the extrusion system on a regular basis.

Poor plasticization of the extrudate. The plasticization issue was mentioned earlier in the discussion of temperature control requirements. Poor plasticization generally appears as: a toad-skin texture on the extruded layer; a dull surface without gloss; and fine cracks.

2. How to handle faults when the extrusion machine is in production

The extrudate temperature is too low; too much filling compound overflows; the production line speed is too high, causing the sheath to be cooled too rapidly; the hot water trough temperature is too low and the trough is positioned too close to the die; the draw ratio of the die set is too small, or the die set is unreasonable, causing a loose sheath; and the melting point of the composite film of the longitudinally applied tape is too high. Based on the above causes, pay attention to the die configuration requirements and, where necessary, make adjustments according to the cable core. Do not let the sheath cool down too rapidly, so as to improve the bonding strength; do not lower the die head temperature excessively in an attempt to improve the sheath's dimensional stability; and control the filling amount of the compound. Ideally, when you lightly touch the cable core with a finger, a thin layer of compound can be scraped off.

The appearance of the extruded sheath fails to meet the standard. This appears specifically as scratches on the surface of the extruded layer; roughness with pinholes or micro-cracks; or any defect caused by poor plasticization. The main causes are: improper selection of the extrusion die sleeve. If it is too small, a rough, rippled surface results; if it is too large, gaps or loose extrusion occur; and if foreign matter is stuck in the die sleeve, it scratches the sheath surface.

If the die head heating temperature is too high, the surface becomes rough; if it is too low, micro-cracks appear. Damage in the sizing zone of the die sleeve, or the sheath being scratched inside the water trough, can also cause defects. For the above causes, the defects can be eliminated or prevented during production. In actual production, besides the defects and causes mentioned above, there are also problems such as take-up winding issues, longitudinal wrapping overlap width problems, and bamboo-joint-shaped appearance. If we observe and summarize more during production and grasp the main, essential causes of the problems, they will be solved and the quality of the cable can be improved further.

news_show-29.html.html:
For stranding on a stranding machine, if it is concentric layer stranding, the first thing to consider is whether the number and size of the pay-off reels of the stranding machine are suitable for it; the second is the direction of lay, the lay length, and whether the wires need to be untwisted. For a multi-wire stranded conductor, the deformation of the stranded wire must also be considered. The strand structure, specification and material should be analyzed and the process data determined before finally selecting a suitable stranding machine. For buncher products, besides the number and size of the pay-off reels, determining the size of the take-up reel is far more important than it is for stranding machines.

If there is no strict requirement on how large the pay-off reel for a coarse single wire should be, order according to the specified length - fine wires use small reels and coarse wires use large reels.

Generally speaking, the speed of a cage-type twisting machine is far lower than that of a fork-type stranding machine, and the speed of a fork-type stranding machine is far lower than that of a tubular-type twisting machine. Another point is that the common twin-twist machine takes the form of a floating double-twist cradle.

How to do a good job of self-inspection of the stranded output?

For an enterprise, the normal operation of the machine is very necessary. To make the finished products look better, deliver better quality, and minimize losses caused by human factors, the following work should be done well while the stranding machine is in use:

1. Check that the stranded conductor from the preceding process is not reddened or blackened;

2. Confirm that the wire count and direction from the preceding process are correct, the marking is complete and the connections are neat;

3. Verify that the packaging is intact and that the marking and specification meet the process requirements;

4. Check whether the actual production operation complies with the requirements of the process card;

5. Check that the stranded wire is round in appearance, well compacted and well formed, with no missing wires, jumping wires or missing wrapping;

6. Check that the loading of this process meets the loading requirements, the reel is intact, and the take-up winding is neat.

Causes of wrong stranding direction and disordered cable arrangement on the stranding machine, and how to eliminate them. During use, due to improper operation or other natural factors, the stranding machine may produce wrong stranding direction, unqualified lay length, disordered take-up winding, or wire compression.

Wrong lay direction and unqualified lay length (mainly too large) are mainly caused by judgment errors. Operators should strengthen their sense of responsibility during operation, work strictly in accordance with the process card, and step up in-process inspection to prevent the production of human-caused rejects and waste. If the take-up arrangement is disordered with wire compression, it is basically caused by the following: stranded products are generally supplied on reels. Large cross-sections should be arranged one by one, and in particular the bottom layers must be arranged neatly. When the wire is traversed or the direction is reversed, because of the one-time stop, pay special attention to ensuring that there is no excessive gap between the upper and lower layers; the lay spacing should be appropriate, otherwise wire compression is likely to occur.

To deal with the above situations, the following measures can be taken:

First, adjust the take-up tension well. When laying out cables manually, it is recommended to arrange them in a flexible manner. Second, the spacing of the cable arrangement should vary according to the diameter of the core wires. Laying out the first layer is the key, and it must be arranged neatly. For the following layers, manual wiring is needed when adjusting each layer to ensure the wiring quality. Third, strengthen the sense of operational responsibility, observe the cable laying quality at any time, and adjust promptly whenever problems are found. Also pay attention to securing the two wire ends and the edge spacing.

The stranding principle and the definition of lay length of the stranding machine:

The stranding machine is a wire and cable machine used for stranding core wires such as power cords, earphone wires and electronic wires. The main stranding principle is: when the copper wires pass through the stranding bow of the stranding machine, the bow causes each individual copper wire to be wrapped helically through circular motion. Copper wires of different specifications and counts are twisted together in a certain arrangement order and at a certain lay, forming a conductor of larger diameter. This stranded conductor is much softer than a single copper wire of the same diameter, and the wires made from it also have better bending performance.

Definition of the lay of the stranding machine. Each individual wire appears once at a fixed distance along the stranding direction; this fixed distance is the lay length of the strand (pitch for short). Another definition of lay: it refers to the vertical distance that the stranded wire advances after being rotated 360 degrees around the stranding axis.

A bunched wire is formed by twisting multiple single wires together. Generally, the individual wires in a bunched conductor are many and fine, which increases the flexibility of the wire and cable and improves the reliability of the circuit connection. To achieve better flexibility or higher reliability, the conductors of some wires and cables are twisted. To bunch or twist the single wires at a certain helix angle (or lay), the machine must meet the following requirements: first, all the single wires should rotate around the central axis of the machine; second, the twisted product should advance in a straight line. By changing the coordination of these two motions, the helix angle can be adjusted so that the stranded wire or bunched wire produced meets the structural requirements.

The stranding machine consists of the pay-off unit, the haul-off unit, the traverse and take-up unit, the drive and transmission system, and the control system. In addition, there are devices such as separating plates, combining dies (also called pressing dies) and length counters.

The stranding machine produces stranded wire of relatively large specification. When stranding, apart from the central single wire, the pay-off reels of the remaining single wires are all placed in the pay-off section (such as the cage). Through its rotation, the single wires form a stranded layer around the central wire. According to the number of stranded layers and the number of single wires in each layer, stranding machines generally have several (or several sections of) pay-off parts that rotate separately, so that stranded wire with a different lay direction in each layer can be produced; it is therefore especially suitable for producing concentric layer stranded wire. The bunched wire produced by a bunching machine is of small specification. It is formed by the rotation of the basket frame or rotating body in the take-up section. Because all the running actions of the bunching machine take place in the take-up section, with the change gear mechanism installed inside the rotating basket frame where space is limited, the bunching machine can only produce twisted products of one lay direction and smaller specification. However, the number of single wires to be bunched can be flexibly configured as required.

What is a pay-off stand? How many types of pay-off stands are there?

The pay-off stand is a widely used auxiliary machine in the wire and cable industry, and it performs the pay-off function for the stranding machine.

Generally, according to power transmission, pay-off stands can be divided into:

active pay-off stands and passive pay-off stands. By style, pay-off stands can be divided into vertical pay-off stands and horizontal pay-off stands. By axis mode, they can be divided into axial pay-off stands and shaftless pay-off stands.

Common pay-off stands include active pay-off stands, vertical power pay-off stands, twin-shaft power pay-off stands, twin-shaft multi-head tray-type active pay-off stands, shaftless pay-off stands, shaftless take-up stands, passive pay-off stands, and others.

The above is about the stranding machine process flow and common fault troubleshooting methods.

The cage stranding machine is a new type of machine that has developed rapidly in recent years. For imported models, the design typically selects a programmable controller as the key control device for the machinery and equipment. The cage stranding machine offers high production efficiency and greatly reduces reliance on manual labor; it is especially suitable for production and processing sites with high output. As is well known, this machine model integrates many new technologies such as CNC machine tools, pneumatics and optical switches. In addition, the operating technicians can monitor several such machines at the same time, and the manufacturing quality is relatively stable. Because the cage stranding machine and its parts use many non-standard and customized components, the whole maintenance process is quite complex, and the repair cycle becomes longer when problems occur.

1. Coil specification problem

When winding a single turn with the cage stranding machine, the current of the magnetic powder clutch that controls the tension of the high-speed cage winding machine is set to 0.45 A. After the coil is wound, the specification of the B end is slightly larger, beyond the process requirements.

2. Cause analysis of the coil specification problem

It was found that if the current related to the tension resistance of the cage stranding machine is set to 0.45 A, the tension resistance during winding is too small, causing non-uniform force on the wire in the winding drum. The wire between the upper drum and the wire seat is not ideally horizontal but loose and tilted, so when the drum rotates, due to inertia, the drum speed is high and the wire slips more, resulting in uneven support of the wire in the winding, insufficient tightness of the coil, and the B end coil exceeding the technical requirements.

The cage stranding machine is a widely used model and specification, also known as the CNC automatic winding machine. It can wire automatically and can perform different winding resistance adjustments according to the mechanical system. Many manufacturers have made innovations in terms of function and use. After upgrades, the range of products in use continues to expand. As a common model on the market, it has advantages such as high efficiency, easy maintenance and good value for money. It has long been a very refined machine model, and its price is far lower than that of the countless automatic chain-movement machines actually used.

Production precautions for cage stranding machine wire:

1. The bare copper wire should be of good standard, neatly arranged, round and smooth, bright on the surface, and free of oxidation.

2. The electrical configuration and instrument displays of the machine should be normal, the rotating parts should run smoothly, and there should be no loose parts.

3. Adjust the drawing tension to a suitable value according to the specification of the stranded steel wire.

4. Select the middle copper wire to pass through the counting needle.

5. Thread the wires reasonably and separately from the wire clamp plate, and adjust the wire clamp plate and the stranding die to suitable positions.

6. Select a suitable pressing die to ensure that the copper wire is smooth with no jumping strands or scratches.

7. The rollers that the copper wire passes through should rotate flexibly, and there should be no loose copper wire at any roller.

8. There should be no foreign matter inside the machine, the take-up machine should be firmly installed, and the protective signal feedback (sensor detector) should be intact.

The above introduces the common problems and production process of the cage stranding machine. If you want to know more, please feel free to contact us at any time.

Every operator must understand that reducing the frequency of maintenance and part replacement for the extrusion machine and increasing its working service life are the key concrete measures for lowering the cost of plastic products and improving economic efficiency. Being able to keep the machine working at its best for a long time, with stable plastic quality and output, is the basic condition for ensuring that a production enterprise enjoys relatively high profits.

Operators who can carry out their self-managed work according to the safety operating procedures and stay committed to their jobs give the equipment the best maintenance and care. Therefore, before new workers take up their posts, they must first learn and memorize the safety operating procedures of the extrusion machine; only after passing the operating process assessment can they officially come on duty and work independently.

To work independently and become a qualified extrusion machine production operator, the following matters need attention:

(1) At shift handover, remind the next shift of the problems caused by this shift's production line equipment and hand over the details clearly; keep proper handover records of the total output of this shift, the product quality and the safety instruments used in production.

(2) At shift takeover, after completing the handover procedures, first check the production quality of the equipment, check the quality of the raw materials used for manufacturing, and check the quantity of materials in the extrusion machine hopper. If any problem is found, immediately report it to the supervisor.

(3) Check whether the temperature of the extrusion machine barrel and the process control environment is within the manufacturing standard processing temperature range. You can adjust it moderately according to the product quality and your own practical experience.

(4) Walk a full inspection lap around the production line equipment to check the working condition of each transmission part while the equipment is running, see whether the operation is stable and normal, listen for any abnormal noise at work, and check whether the ambient temperature of the heating position is working normally.

(5) Look at the gauges to check the main motor working voltage and ammeter on the actual operation control cabinet. At this time, the ammeter pointer should be within the normal rated voltage value range.

(6) Production is running normally. While the extrusion machine screw is rotating steadily, the plastic products are being extruded at a uniform, stable speed by the machine; from time to time, check the appearance quality of the equipment, or take some products to check whether the equipment indicators are qualified.

(7) In the event of a sudden power failure during work, immediately turn off the power switches of the main motor, electric heating and feeding system, and turn the knob of the variable speed switch to the zero position. When the power supply is restored, first heat the barrel, and after the processing temperature is reached, hold the temperature for a period of time. Manually turn the motor drive belt to test the rotational force of the screw; if it turns relatively easily, run the motor at low speed and start working. If the ammeter pointer exceeds the rated voltage value or the screw speed ratio is unstable, stop immediately, find out the cause (it may be that the material temperature in the barrel is low), investigate and eliminate the fault according to the rules, and only then restart.

(8) If the machine is stopped for a long time or production is suspended, and the material inside the barrel is a polyolefin-based raw material, it does not need to be removed. If the barrel contains acrylic resin or other materials, the material in the barrel needs to be removed; then disassemble the screw and remove the adhered material from the screw and the barrel; after the finished products inside the screw and barrel are cleaned, coat a layer of rust preventive, wrap the screw, and hang it vertically in dry, well-ventilated conditions.

It is hoped that all operators will follow the above principles when using the extrusion machine, so as to reduce enterprise costs and improve efficiency.

1. Before starting work, put on protective gear, and wear no more than two gloves on each hand.

2. Be familiar with the machine performance and operating techniques. You may participate in operating the stranding machine after arrangement or approval by the team leader; apprentices must operate under the guidance of skilled workers.

3. Before starting the machine, check whether the mechanical and electrical quantities are normal. If there is any fault, eliminate it in time; otherwise do not start the machine. Pay attention to the lubrication and cleaning of the equipment, and do not add oil while the machine is running to avoid danger. 5. When the coil is placed into the stranding machine, immediately lock the locking device; otherwise, the coil may become loose and cause equipment and personal accidents. Before starting the machine, close the protective guard, and make sure there are no obstacles within the rotating range of the machine before starting.

6. The protective guard may be opened only when the machine has come to a complete stop. Working on the machine is prohibited. When the machine is rotating, stepping on the machine is prohibited.

7. Operators should care for and look after each other. Before starting the machine, they must sound the alarm and confirm it is safe before starting.

8. If any abnormal sound is heard from the running machine, stop immediately for inspection, and restart only after the obstacle is removed.

9. Operators should check the butt welding machine; the welder must have a grounding wire, and eye protection should be used during operation.

10. Disconnect the power supply after stopping.

2. Faults that can occur with the cable stranding machine

During the whole application process of the cable stranding machine, due to unscientific operation or other natural factors, the twisting direction of the cable stranding machine may become wrong, the twisting lay diameter may be unqualified, or even disordered take-up winding and wire compression may occur.

Wrong twisting direction and unqualified twisting lay diameter (mainly slightly too large) are mainly caused by judgment errors, including errors in judging the twisting direction. During the operation, the operators should strengthen their sense of responsibility, strictly execute the process card, improve roving inspection, and avoid rejects and waste caused by human factors.

If the wiring is disordered or wires are compressed, it is mostly caused by the following situations: stranded products are generally supplied on trays. Large cross-sections should be arranged one by one, and especially the bottom wire must be arranged neatly. When the cable reverses its traversing direction, because of the one-time stop, special attention should be paid to ensuring there is no very large gap between the upper and lower layers, and the arrangement spacing should be suitable. If it is too large, wire compression is easily caused.

For the above situations, we can choose the following methods to handle them:

First, adjust the take-up tension of the cable stranding machine. When the cables are arranged manually, the most suitable method is to arrange them flexibly.

Second, according to the core diameter specification, adjust the lay diameter of the cable. Arranging the first layer is the key, and it must be arranged neatly. For the following layers, manpower should be arranged when adjusting each layer to ensure the arrangement quality.

Third, improve the sense of responsibility during operation, observe the cable laying quality at any time, and adjust immediately when problems are found. Pay attention to fixing the two wire ends and the edge spacing.

Maintenance and care of the cage stranding machine.

When the cage stranding machine is running, pay attention to the lubrication of the transmission parts in each section, and add lubricating oil once every 10 days of production, so as to avoid wear of the rotating parts due to lack of lubricating oil.

Long-term use with the wire drum between the pulling friction wheel and the bevel gear can cause damage to the rotating bearing; replace damaged bearings at any time.

Long-term use of the friction transmission will wear out the friction pads and discs; replace them promptly. The friction discs should be re-machined to restore the surface profile, so that the friction coefficient meets the friction and sliding requirements, ensuring that the disc works normally and drives the take-up shaft to rotate.

For mica tape wrapping on the wrapping machine, it is difficult to give definitive figures for how many layers should be wrapped and what the overlap rate should be. Generally, mica tape manufacturers recommend wrapping 2 layers, with the overlap rate equal to or slightly greater than 50%.

Because cable products differ in material properties and model/specification, only the product designer can give definitive values for how many layers to wrap or how much overlap is needed to pass the fire-resistance test, based on the results of repeated tests. Of course, the more wrapping layers, the higher the product pass rate, and vice versa. However, this not only wastes mica tape - it also increases the insulation and sheath outer diameter of the cable, which in turn raises the plastic quota, increases manufacturing cost, and reduces the competitiveness of the product. The number of wrapping layers should therefore be determined by the user's requirements, the cable structure, the complexity of the process, the voltage class and the test results.

Meanwhile, with a given number of wrapping layers, the overlap rate is also a very important indicator, because it determines the actual number of wrapping layers. For example, if one layer is wrapped with an overlap rate of 50%, the actual number of wrapping layers is 2. If the overlap rate is below 50% - say 25% - the actual wrapping layer is 1.5, meaning some places have 2 layers and others have 1 layer. Obviously, the 1-layer positions are liable to breakdown. If two layers of mica tape are wrapped with overlap rates both below 50%, the single-layer positions of the inner and outer wrap layers may overlap each other, so that those positions actually have only two layers of mica tape and are therefore more liable to breakdown than positions with four layers.

In process terms, it is very difficult to achieve an overlap rate of exactly 50%. In actual use, bending and other factors can also cause the overlap rate to fall below 50%. Therefore, in actual production, the overlap rate should be controlled at slightly greater than 50%.

The above is what the wrapping machine has explained about the number of wrapping layers and the overlap rate; we hope it is helpful to you.
